bg.note: Page background (--bg), dark theme default; also --header-bg, the text on every line colour (--on-line-1/2/3) and on the action ink (--accent-text).

line-1.note: Line 1 only: track, stations, bullet, band stretch, chip dots. Also --term-key on the code panel.

line-2.note: Line 2 only: track, stations, bullet, band stretch, chip dots. Also --term-number on the code panel.

line-3.note: Line 3 only: track, stations, bullet, band stretch, chip dots, and the 404 line.

line-neutral.note: --line-neutral: track, stations and end bars of the diagrams that belong to no job; their stations are filled with --line-neutral-fill (#f3f4f6). They never glow.

accent.note: --accent, --btn-bg, --progress: primary button, links, nav underline, palette ring, brand mark. Text on it is --accent-text (#0e1013).

ok.note: --ok: the 200 OK chip and done dots. Also --term-string on the code panel.

danger.note: --danger: error states only, apart from Magenta Line 3.

grid-dot.note: --grid-dot: a 1px dot every 22px behind the page, fixed while it scrolls; the only background texture.

packet.note: --packet: the data packets of the hero map; --packet-halo (#ffffff40) draws their small halo in the dark theme only.

term-bg.note: JSON code panel (--term-bg), dark in both themes.

term-text.note: Code text (--term-text); keys Cyan #00a7db, strings Green #5fd39a, numbers and literals Orange #f39700, punctuation #959ca6.

bg-light.note: Also the text on the light action ink (--accent-text).

surface-light.note: Also the light interchange fill and the light --line-neutral-fill.

text-light.note: Also the light --focus, interchange stroke and action ink.

display.purpose: The hero name only; Barlow Condensed 700, solid text colour.

headline.purpose: Every h2 section head, uppercase, with the band of line colours under it.

headline-sm.purpose: Signs inside a block and CV section signs, uppercase.

title.purpose: h3 and band titles in Barlow 600.

body-sm.purpose: Points, legend entries, palette rows; nav links at 500.

chip.purpose: Technology chips and filter chips, in the mono face: technologies are data.

data.purpose: Periods on the route and the screen CV, project counts, shortcut keys; JetBrains Mono. The printed CV keeps Barlow.

label.purpose: Uppercase group labels in the command palette.

map-sign.purpose: Station and interchange labels in SVG viewBox units, JetBrains Mono; hubs 700 13px, NOW 700 18px, years 12px; larger on the compact map. Placed for 0.6 em a character.

mono.purpose: JSON view, request bar, palette target paths.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Sticky filter status bar, mobile menu panel, skip link.

motion.name: t-hover
motion.purpose: Colour, border and background transitions on hover and focus.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Standard ease for the JSON view's line entrance.

motion.name: packet-run
motion.value: linear infinite, 8s-14s per run (track length / 80 units per second)
motion.purpose: The single ambient loop: one white data packet per line on the hero map, with a small halo in the dark theme, staggered, paused off screen, pausable, removed under reduced motion; the static glow of the tracks stays.

motion.name: night-city
motion.value: 7.5s opening shot, then damped camera and endless scene time
motion.purpose: The 3D night city of the full and lite levels: trains, traffic trails, light streams, the beam and rings of "Now", the drone drift. Drawn only while seen, stopped by the pause button, absent under reduced motion and Save-Data, where the page is the flat map.

motion.name: json-line
motion.purpose: One-shot entrance of the JSON body when the view opens; only with no reduced-motion preference.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Global under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce; smooth scrolling also off.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Wider gutters (24px) and section padding (56px), tablet hero, two-column table.

breakpoints.name: split-404
breakpoints.purpose: 404 page only: languages side by side.

breakpoints.name: nav
breakpoints.purpose: Full header nav replaces the mobile menu.

breakpoints.name: desktop
breakpoints.purpose: Wide map, three-column table, alternating focus bands.

narrative.overview:
The site is drawn as a schematic transit map at night. A career is a network: each employer is a coloured line, numbered by start date; each project is a station on its line; every technology used at two employers or more is an interchange where their lines meet, and all lines converge on a shared terminus labelled "Now". These relationships are computed from the experience data, and the build stops when a hand-placed map no longer matches that data, so the drawing is a record, not an illustration. Map language (lines, stations, end bars, legend, "not to scale") reaches every block, from the route of the experience section to the CV sheet and the 404 page.

The material is a graphite signal board: flat graphite panels with 1px rules over a fine dot grid fixed behind the page, and, in the dark theme only, tracks lit like the lamps of a dispatch board. Colour is scarce and semantic: three line colours, each owned by one job and used for nothing else; actions are drawn in ink, the text colour of the theme. Type is split into signs, text and data: condensed capitals for the name and section signs; a plain sans for anything a person reads; JetBrains Mono for data (map labels, dates, counts, technology chips, shortcut keys) and code. Density is moderate and reading-first: a recruiter must find role, stack and contact without decoding the map, and every map has a plain equivalent (accessible SVG title and description, the route list, the interchange table).

Motion is one quiet loop: small white data packets running along the hero map's lines, paused off screen, paused by a button, and absent under reduced motion. Where the device allows it, the same network also stands as a miniature city at night in 3D (see Night City 3D), on phones as on desktops: lit towers, a river, metro viaducts, trains running into "Now", and a drone camera that follows the page. Without WebGL 2, under reduced motion or with Save-Data, the page is exactly the flat map. The world rejects the generic dark developer portfolio: no gradient name, frosted stat tiles, comment-style labels, numbered sections, blobs or glowing text. On the flat page light belongs to the tracks alone; in the 3D city it belongs to the city and to the lines.
keyCharacteristics: Three line colours (cyan, orange, magenta) belong to the lines only; actions are ink, never a line colour.
Tracks run only horizontally, vertically or at 45°, with rounded bends and square end bars; in the dark theme they glow.
Stations are rings on the page background; interchanges are light capsules with an ink edge.
Barlow Condensed for signs, Barlow for text, JetBrains Mono for data and code.
Flat graphite surfaces with 1px edges over a fixed dot grid; soft black shadow only on layers that float over content.
Dark is the default theme; light is an explicit visitor choice; print is pure black on white.

The 3D night city is progressive: its metro is built from the same data. At the full level it stands behind the whole home page, beside platform panels on wide windows and between glass cards on phones; on weak devices it falls back to the hero map box (lite level). The flat page is its off level.

rules.name: The Three Lines Rule
rules.body: The line colours belong to the lines and to nothing else. Each belongs to one job in start order (line 1 = first job) and appears only where that line is meant: track, station, bullet, band stretch, its chip dots, and the 404 line. Status, actions and diagrams that belong to no job have colours of their own. In the 3D city a line colour appears only on parts of its line: the LED strips of its viaduct, the stripe of its trains, its portal, hologram and light stream, its ring at "Now" and the tags of its stations; the city's own lights are white, warm, or the red beacons of the towers.

rules.name: The Action Ink Rule
rules.body: Every action is drawn in ink (`--accent` / `--accent-text`): the primary button, links, the "Show n more" fold, the current nav underline, the palette ring and underline, the brand mark. Signal White with graphite text in dark, near-black with light text in light; never a line colour.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Line Rule
rules.body: Text on a line colour takes the `--on-line-N` of that line: ink #0e1013 on all three in dark; white on all three in light. Body text never takes a line colour unless it passes 4.5:1 on its surface (JSON tokens sit on the dark code panel for that reason).

rules.name: The Lit Tracks Rule
rules.body: Light belongs to the tracks. In the dark theme only, the tracks and end bars of a job's line glow like the lamps of a dispatch board on the hero map, the terminus sign and the 404 map: two blurred copies of the track under it, about 4px and 10px, the outer one at 45% (class `.led`, filter `#led` in `src/components/metro/LedGlow.astro`). In the 3D city the light comes from the scene itself (windows, street lamps, trains, the LED strips of the viaducts and the light layer of portals, holograms, streams and the beam) under a moderate bloom, dark theme only. Data packets are white with a small halo. Text, buttons, cards and the neutral diagrams never glow, nor does anything in the light theme or in print. No gradients, frosted glass, backdrop blur or coloured shadows, apart from the surfaces of the full 3D level: platform panels, phone cards, the soft backdrop behind the hero name block and the glass tags of the scene (see Elevation & Depth); the older tokens (`--grad`, `--glass`, `--glow*`, `--grid-line`, `--hero-glow*`, `--grad-rail`, `--accent-2/3`) resolve to a flat colour, transparent or none and must never be re-inflated.

rules.name: The Dot Grid Rule
rules.body: One background texture only: a 1px dot every 22px in `--grid-dot`, fixed behind the page while it scrolls. No square grid, no noise; every block with a background of its own covers it. The 3D city brings its own ground (roads, pavements, parks, the river); the dot grid stays the texture of the page wherever the scene is not drawn.

rules.name: The Sign Face Rule
rules.body: Barlow Condensed is for signs only: the name, section signs (uppercase), company names at line starts, route numerals, the "Now" sign of the route, diagram labels. Body headings from h3 down, UI controls and running text stay in Barlow.

rules.name: The Data Mono Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono marks data and code: map labels and years, "You are here", dates and periods, project counts, technology chips, shortcut keys, the JSON view. Names, titles, running text and company names never take it, and the printed CV keeps Barlow. Map labels are placed for 0.6 em a mono character; an interchange name too long for the map takes a shorter label there ("JPA / Hibernate"), its link keeps the full name.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Dates, periods, years, counts and kbd keys use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` (mono figures are tabular already). Headings use `text-wrap: balance`, paragraphs `text-wrap: pretty`.

rules.name: The 45-Degree Rule
rules.body: Every track, on any map or diagram, bends only at 45° or 90°. Parallel lines keep a constant 12px gap and converge in route order.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Panels, sheets, rows and buttons are flat with a 1px edge. A shadow appears only on something that floats over content, is soft and black, and is removed in print.

dos: **Do** draw every new diagram with the map parts (Track, Station, Interchange, Terminal) and the 45-Degree Rule: 7px tracks, 3px station rings on the page background, capsules with a 2px ink edge, square end bars; a diagram that belongs to no job leaves out the route number and draws in `--line-neutral`, so it does not glow.
**Do** take a line's colour from its route number (`--line-1`, `--line-2`, `--line-3`), and derive any new interchange or relationship from the experience data, never by hand.

**Do** put the `--on-line-N` text of the line on any line-colour fill, draw every action in ink (`--accent` / `--accent-text`), and check every new text pair for 4.5:1 in both themes (3:1 for large text, tracks and stations).
**Do** set data in JetBrains Mono (map labels, dates, counts, chips, keys) and place map labels for 0.6 em a character, clear of the tracks, of each other and of the map frame.
**Do** open each home block with the section sign: condensed uppercase headline and the 6px band of related line colours.
**Do** keep touch targets at least 44px, extending a smaller visual (32px chip) with an invisible `::after` rather than enlarging it.

**Do** keep interaction feedback to colour and border changes at 150ms ease-out, with the 2px text-colour focus outline at 3px offset; a pressed filter control inverts to text-colour fill; where the ink equals the text colour, hover underlines instead.
**Do** keep dark as the default theme regardless of OS preference, and give every block a black-on-white print state.
**Do** use Barlow at 400, 500 and 600 only; 700 belongs to the condensed face.

**Do** keep the 3D city a progressive layer: its metro built from the same data and line tokens as the SVG map, fetched only after load, drawn only while it is seen, falling back to lite on weak or slow devices, and leaving the page exactly as it is at the off level.
donts: **Don't** use gradients, frosted glass, backdrop blur, coloured shadows, blobs, noise or a square background grid; the dot grid is the only texture. The surfaces of the full 3D level (platform panels, phone cards, the hero backdrop and the scene tags) are the only translucent, blurred ones.
**Don't** put a glow on text, buttons, cards or the neutral diagrams, or anywhere in the light theme or in print; inside the 3D scene only its own lights and the faint halo of its tags glow.
**Don't** put a kicker or eyebrow label above a heading, number sections (01–04), or use comment-style labels such as `// about`.
**Don't** set names, titles, running text or company names in mono; mono is for data and code.
**Don't** add another hue or use a line colour for something that is not its line: actions are ink, status is green or red, unowned diagrams are neutral grey.

**Don't** add scroll reveals, count-ups, typing effects or looping decoration; content is visible on load. The packet loop and the 3D city (trains, traffic, streams, the beam, the drone's drift), all stopped by the pause button and absent under reduced motion, stay the only ambient motion.
**Don't** nest cards inside cards or box content that reads as a list; use rules and bands.
**Don't** draw a track segment at any angle other than 0°, 45° or 90°, or label a map relationship the data does not contain.
